sources.title: Ciudades donde opera DiDi en México
sources.proves: Official inventory explicitly lists Acapulco, Ensenada, Guaymas, La Paz, Manzanillo, Mazatlán, Puerto Escondido and Puerto Vallarta. It does not list Los Cabos or Cabo San Lucas.

sources.title: Ya puedes pedir un taxi con DiDi en Puerto Escondido
sources.proves: DiDi Taxi launched in Puerto Escondido with Oaxaca state-government coordination; page shows last update 2025-01-28.

sources.title: Tarifas
sources.proves: Live fare selector exposes passenger routes La Paz–Topolobampo and La Paz–Mazatlán in both directions; displayed one-way La Paz–Topolobampo adult fare MXN 2,000, child/senior MXN 1,000, infant free.
sources.notes: Dynamic fares; recheck before economics lock.

sources.title: Rutas y Horarios
sources.proves: Official schedule selector lists La Paz–Topolobampo and La Paz–Mazatlán in both directions, establishing current operator route availability.
sources.notes: Rendered scraper did not expose actual departure days; service-days remain null.

sources.title: Programa Maestro de Desarrollo Portuario del Puerto de Mazatlán 2025–2030
sources.proves: Official plan identifies the terminal de transbordadores and cruise-passenger plaza; reports 2023 cruise traffic 128 ships/468,969 passengers and transbordador traffic 306 ships/99,407 passengers.

sources.title: Programa Institucional ASIPONA Ensenada 2025–2030
sources.proves: Official series reports 2024 cruise traffic of 272 arrivals and 949,287 passengers; also states marinas/embarcaderos support smaller tourist craft and 60–70% occupancy.
sources.notes: One narrative fragment elsewhere in the same PDF says 353 ships/744.2k passengers for 2024 and conflicts with the repeated statistical series. Use 949,287 only provisionally and flag reconciliation.

sources.title: Preguntas Frecuentes (Atención al Cliente)
sources.proves: Official port page confirms a cruise terminal is part of the Port of Ensenada.

sources.title: Acerca del Puerto
sources.proves: Official port page confirms three cruise berths, specialized maritime-passenger infrastructure, more than 525,000 annual cabotage-tourism users (page vintage unclear), three tourist marinas/524 slips, and 240,000+ cruise passengers in 2014.
sources.notes: Quantitative cabotage figure is not route-specific and page appears partly 2014-vintage.

sources.title: Yelapa, the tropical paradise that you cannot miss
sources.proves: Yelapa is reached by water taxi from Los Muertos Pier or Boca de Tomatlán.

sources.title: Las Animas Beach
sources.proves: Las Ánimas is accessible by panga/water taxi from Los Muertos Pier or Boca de Tomatlán.

sources.title: Fun Starts at the Cabo San Lucas Marina
sources.proves: Confirms Cabo San Lucas Marina as a real marina and center for marine excursions.

sources.title: Beyond the Bridge
sources.proves: Names Marina Puerto Los Cabos as an actual reception/departure setting in San José del Cabo.

sources.title: ASIPONA Acapulco
sources.proves: Official site identifies Terminal Marítima in central Acapulco.

sources.title: La ASIPONA Acapulco da la bienvenida al crucero Norwegian Jade
sources.proves: Documents a current passenger call at Muelle Tramo 1 with 2,126 passengers and 1,019 crew.

sources.title: Typical boat with glass bottom to La Roqueta Island
sources.proves: Commercial operator advertises daily Monday–Sunday glass-bottom boat operation to La Roqueta, with specified holiday non-operation dates.
sources.notes: Operator evidence, not authority confirmation of exact public dock/landing or fare.

sources.title: Casi 58 mil visitantes en cruceros llegaron a Manzanillo en 2025
sources.proves: Official 2025 totals: 18 cruise calls, 39,907 passengers, 17,832 crew; cruise terminal is at the antiguo Muelle Fiscal.

sources.title: PMDP de los puertos de Manzanillo, San Pedrito y Laguna de Cuyutlán 2026–2031
sources.proves: Official plan identifies tourist-cruise terminal infrastructure in Manzanillo/San Pedrito.

sources.title: Da inicio nueva ruta de cabotaje Guaymas–Santa Rosalía
sources.proves: Official launch evidence for Guaymas–Santa Rosalía, initially three trips weekly.
sources.notes: Historic launch only; does not prove 2026 operation.

sources.title: Tu conexión entre la zona central del Golfo de California y B.C.S.
sources.proves: Operator site claims Guaymas–Santa Rosalía passenger/vehicle service and reports 371 trips plus 2,131 passengers and vehicles over ten years.
sources.notes: No visible freshness/service date; 2025 reporting said reopening had no date. Treat current operation as unconfirmed.

sources.title: Isla de Piedra
sources.proves: Tourism source names Embarcadero Isla de la Piedra “Gabriel Leyva” and states the lancha crossing takes five minutes.
sources.notes: Not port-authority/operator evidence; exact destination landing and coordinates still need confirmation.

brief_maturity.method: Field-by-field audit of canonical neutral briefs; recommend additive edits only.

field_scores.finding: Canonical Mexico cluster and two Pacific city IDs are stable; preserve.
Strong two-coast framing but this lane needs a Pacific sub-section rather than replacing the national brief.
Uses broad “millions” and luxury/resort assertions without route-level passenger/fare records.
Good archetypes; Pacific routes require precise public-terminal grounding.
Route IDs resolve, but Pacific signature endpoints include weak/non-public BP labels.
Directionally correct SEMAR framing; add exact port/capitanía/concession requirements per operating port.
Useful broad seasonal note but not tied to local sea-state/service cancellations.
Only two broad URLs; Pacific claims need authority/operator sources.

recommended_enhancements: Add a partner-neutral “Mexico Pacific public-terminal/ferry network” paragraph covering Puerto Vallarta, Mazatlán, La Paz/Pichilingue, Ensenada, Acapulco, Manzanillo and Guaymas as researched/backlog by maturity.
Replace unsourced route-volume language with the demand records in this artifact only after reconciliation and economics approval.
Keep partner-specific DiDi framing out of the canonical brief.

findings: All three source entries are labels without URLs.
Cabo↔La Paz / Espíritu Santo distance and service framing require route/chart verification.

SCT/API wording should be updated to current SEMAR/ASIPONA/capitanía structure.
recommended_enhancements: Add authoritative URLs for Cabo San Lucas Marina and Marina Puerto Los Cabos.
Separate public BPs from beach/resort POIs.

findings: Strong neutral Banderas Bay thesis and current-route evidence.
Approximate distances are attributed only to “nautical chart.”
Current map includes residences, restaurants, beach clubs and generic Water Taxi labels as BPs.
Official tourism sources validate Los Muertos/Boca origins and Yelapa/Las Ánimas corridors.
recommended_enhancements: Ground public water-taxi origins at Los Muertos Pier and Boca de Tomatlán.
Move private-property/restaurant endpoints out of public-BP semantics unless landing rights are proven.
Use ASIPONA port-wide 525k cabotage only as a broad signal, not route demand.

partner_narrative_notes.proposed_partner_narrative: DiDi can become the digital first/last-mile layer around Mexico Pacific’s real passenger-water nodes: cruise gates in Ensenada, Mazatlán, Puerto Vallarta, Acapulco and Manzanillo; the Pichilingue–mainland ferry network; and water-taxi gateways in Banderas Bay. Promote exact DiDi-listed cities only when Atlas hierarchy and boarding-point geometry are sealed. Los Cabos remains a country-supported inherited Atlas market, not an exact city-supported DiDi claim.

city_specific_angles.angle: Airport/hotel/urban DiDi handoff to Los Muertos, Boca de Tomatlán, Marina Vallarta and the cruise port; strongest near-term existing-city deepening.
Two-sided DiDi-supported ferry corridor opportunity around passenger terminals; requires new Atlas city bindings and directional pax/fare data.
Cruise-arrival dispatch and curated terminal-to-water experiences; demand is broad cruise flow, not route demand.
Official DiDi Taxi proof supports airport/urban transfer narrative, but maritime node remains brief-only.
Reactivation watchlist; do not market as active ferry integration until operator/ASIPONA confirms current schedule.

partner_narrative_notes.canonical_neutrality_rule: None of this DiDi-specific framing belongs in canonical cluster/city briefs.

do_not_publish: Do not claim DiDi operates in Los Cabos/Cabo San Lucas at city level; only country-supported Atlas inheritance is evidenced here.
Do not add La Paz, Mazatlán, Acapulco, Ensenada, Manzanillo, Guaymas or Puerto Escondido to map footprint until stable Atlas IDs, hierarchy and sealed geometry exist.
Do not treat Harbor 171, Bistro Marina, Ánima Beach Club, Club Ninety Six, OMNIA Dayclub or Cabo Pulmo Sport Center as public boarding points.
Do not publish generic endpoints such as “Los Cabos, Baja Sur” or “Water Taxi” as BPs.
Do not use 525k Puerto Vallarta cabotage tourists, 949,287 Ensenada cruise passengers, or any broad tourism/cruise total as route demand without an explicit capture assumption.
Do not use Mazatlán’s 99,407 transbordador passengers as annual one-way La Paz↔Mazatlán demand; it is aggregate and non-directional.
Do not call Guaymas↔Santa Rosalía current until a dated 2026 operator/authority schedule is verified.
Do not expose routes ics-3b1885b0e5 or ics-c1f5deb1fa as clean Mexico records while cluster_id is incorrectly galapagos-ecuador.
Do not quote Ensenada 2024 cruise figures externally until the source’s 949,287/272 versus 744.2k/353 conflict is reconciled.
Do not edit or replace canonical briefs wholesale; enhancements must be additive and partner-neutral.
